page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a high-performance computing server powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz with one thread per core. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, alongside cryptography standards like VAES and SHA_NI. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include integrated GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the hpc7a.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution and memory bandwidth. The system achieved top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core testing and large-block memory bandwidth, with read speeds reaching 695.05 GB/sec and write speeds at 347.3 GB/sec. It also excels in complex computational tasks, scoring in the top tier for software compilation with Clang, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark physics simulations. However, single-threaded performance is relatively lower, with gzip compression and bzip3 single-threaded decompression registering in the average tier. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hpc7a.24xlarge offers high resource density for parallel computing workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high-speed DDR5 memory bandwidth. The lack of hyperthreading ensures predictable execution times for high-performance computing applications. This profile is highly suitable for scientific simulations, molecular modeling, weather forecasting, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing. It is also capable of handling medium-to-large language model inference, demonstrating strong performance in text generation for 7B and 70B models.
